title_en: Jiangyou City Urban Credit Cooperative Dissolution Liquidation Group v. Sichuan High People's Court — application for confirmation of illegal enforcement conduct
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 31 of the State Compensation Law of the PRC, if a people's court makes an error in executing an effective civil legal document and causes damage, the victim has the right to claim compensation. According to Article 11 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Confirmation Cases of State Compensation by People's Courts (Trial Implementation), to confirm that an execution act is unlawful, it is required that there be an official act (including an omission), that the act be unlawful, and that there be actual damage. In the course of execution, if a people's court corrects an improper substantive handling of an execution ruling by way of correcting a clerical error, although there is a procedural defect, it does not cause actual loss to the legitimate rights of the person seeking confirmation, and the execution act should not be confirmed as unlawful.
keywords_en: state compensation; confirmation of unlawful execution act; retrial; Supreme People's Court; Sichuan Province; legal person; State Compensation Law; Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Confirmation Cases of State Compensation by People's Courts; whether improper substantive handling of execution ruling constitutes unlawfulness; whether correction of clerical error constitutes procedural defect; whether actual loss caused; dismissal of claim; compensation with land use rights; execution auction; creditor's rights distribution; land use rights
full_text_en:
Liquidation Group of Jiangyou City Credit Cooperative v. Sichuan High People's Court — application for confirmation of illegal enforcement

Ruling Summary

In accordance with Article 31 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, if a people's court errs in enforcing an effective civil legal instrument and causes damage, the victim has the right to claim compensation. Pursuant to Article 11 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Confirmation Cases for State Compensation by People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), confirmation that an enforcement act is illegal requires the existence of an official act (including an omission), the illegality of the act, and actual damage results. Where, during the enforcement process, a people's court corrects an error in the substantive handling of an enforcement ruling by means of correcting a clerical error, although there is a procedural defect, it does not cause actual loss to the lawful rights of the applicant for confirmation, and the enforcement act should not be confirmed as illegal.

Ruling of the Supreme People's Court
Case No. (2009) Que Shen Zi No. 1

Applicant for Confirmation: Liquidation Group of Jiangyou City Credit Cooperative, address: 2nd Floor, Taibai Building, Zhongba Town, Jiangyou City, Sichuan Province.
Responsible Person: Hu Debing, Head of the Liquidation Group.
Agent ad litem: Yang Anguo, lawyer at Sichuan United Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Luo Chuanjia, lawyer at Sichuan Fanguo Law Firm.

The applicant for confirmation, the Liquidation Group of Jiangyou City Credit Cooperative (hereinafter referred to as Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group), with respect to its application for confirmation of illegal enforcement by the Sichuan High People's Court, being dissatisfied with the ruling of the Sichuan High People's Court (2009) Chuan Fa Que Zi No. 1, filed a petition with this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to hear the case, and the trial has now concluded.

The reasons given by Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group for applying for confirmation of illegality to the court of first instance were: 1. The Sichuan High People's Court, by ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2, wholly transferred the land use rights and buildings of the execution debtor Chengdu Luoshu Real Estate Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Luoshu Real Estate Company) to Jiangyou City Credit Cooperative (hereinafter referred to as Jiangyou Credit Cooperative), and subsequently, without undergoing trial supervision procedures, directly issued civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2-1 on the grounds of a clerical error, thereby altering the substantive content of the above effective ruling, in violation of Article 88 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Execution Work of People's Courts; 2. The Sichuan High People's Court issued rulings (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2-2 and No. 2-4, arbitrarily disposing of property that had already been ruled to be transferred to Jiangyou Credit Cooperative, in an illegal manner; 3. The appraised value of the execution debtor's property was RMB 31,032,500, but the proceeds from the auction conducted by the Sichuan High People's Court were only RMB 6,000,000, and the reserve price for the auction was not agreed to by Jiangyou Credit Cooperative.

The court of first instance found the following facts: In the loan dispute case between Jiangyou Credit Cooperative and Luoshu Real Estate Company, the Jiangyou City People's Court of Sichuan Province opened a case for trial on May 27, 1998, and issued a ruling to seal up the land use rights of Luoshu Real Estate Company located at Tianyashi South Street, Chengdu, and the buildings in Lianhua Residential Area, Jinjiang District, and Shabanqiao Residential Area, Chenghua District. The case was later transferred to the Sichuan High People's Court for trial pursuant to law, which rendered civil judgment (1998) Chuan Jing Er Chu Zi No. 70 on May 19, 1999, ordering Luoshu Real Estate Company to repay Jiangyou Credit Cooperative the principal of RMB 34,000,000 in loans plus interest. After the judgment became effective, the Sichuan High People's Court, based on the application of Jiangyou Credit Cooperative, opened a case for enforcement on November 17, 1999. On March 1, 2000, Sichuan Zhanwang Industrial Company, holding a notarized creditor's document (2000) Shu Gong Zheng Zi No. 0593 from Sichuan Notary Public Office, also applied to the Sichuan High People's Court for compulsory enforcement of a debt of RMB 3,824,000 owed by Luoshu Real Estate Company. The court opened a case for enforcement on March 9, 2000.

On March 13, 2000, the Sichuan High People's Court commissioned Sichuan Taihua Accounting Firm (later renamed Sichuan Tonghe Accounting Firm) to appraise the sealed-up property of Luoshu Real Estate Company. The appraisal conclusion issued by the firm on March 17, 2000 was: the 7,000.04 square meters of land use rights at Tianyashi South Street were valued at RMB 27,416,200; the 38 buildings in Shabanqiao Residential Area were valued at RMB 2,822,900; and the 11 buildings in Lianhua Residential Area were valued at RMB 793,400; total RMB 31,032,500. The restrictive conditions for the use of the appraisal results were: outstanding land concession fees of RMB 1,653,200, estimated relocation costs of RMB 19,500,000, and the two properties not having been transferred. The appraisal report stated that it was valid for half a year, i.e., from February 29, 2000 to August 28, 2000.

On March 20, 2000, the Sichuan High People's Court issued civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2, transferring the 7,000.04 square meters of land use rights at Tianyashi South Street, the 38 buildings in Shabanqiao Residential Area, Chenghua District, and the 11 buildings in Lianhua Residential Area, Jinjiang District, owned by Luoshu Real Estate Company, to Jiangyou Credit Cooperative as compensation. On the same day, the ruling was served on Jiangyou Credit Cooperative. On April 7, 2000, the Sichuan High People's Court issued civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2-1 on the grounds of correcting a clerical error in ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2, which stated: after the words "commercial housing" on page 2, line 12 of civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2, and before the words "transferred to the execution applicant as compensation," the following should be added: "pending the issuance of an appraisal report and consideration of the distribution to other creditors, the specific amount will be determined later." On the same day, the ruling was served on Jiangyou Credit Cooperative.

On August 14, 2000, the Chengdu Administration for Industry and Commerce of Sichuan Province issued a written certificate to the Sichuan High People's Court stating that Luoshu Real Estate Company had not undergone annual inspection for more than two years and should be deemed to have voluntarily ceased operations.

After the first appraisal report expired, the Sichuan High People's Court again commissioned Sichuan Tonghe Accounting Firm on November 15, 2001 to appraise the sealed-up property of Luoshu Real Estate Company. The appraisal conclusion was: the 7,000.04 square meters of land use rights at Tianyashi South Street were valued at RMB 27,874,400; the 38 buildings in Shabanqiao Residential Area were valued at RMB 2,620,800; total RMB 30,495,200. The 11 buildings in Lianhua Residential Area were not included in the scope of the appraisal. The appraisal report also stated the restrictive conditions for its use.

On November 27, 2001, after soliciting opinions, the Sichuan High People's Court obtained confirmation from the Jiangyou City People's Government that the reserve price for the auction of the land use rights involved was RMB 5,000,000 and for the buildings was RMB 800,000. The Chengdu International Commodity Auction Center, commissioned by the Sichuan High People's Court, conducted two auctions of the land use rights and buildings, but neither was successful. On February 25, 2002, the Sichuan High People's Court again consulted with the Jiangyou City People's Government and the Jiangyou Sub-branch of the People's Bank of China, among others. The Jiangyou City People's Government requested that the auction continue, setting the reserve price for the land use rights at RMB 5,000,000 and for the buildings at RMB 1,000,000. Upon written commission by the Sichuan High People's Court, Sichuan Hanya Cultural Treasures Auction House auctioned the buildings in Shabanqiao Residential Area on March 20, 2002 for RMB 1,000,000, and on April 12 of the same year, auctioned the land use rights at Tianyashi South Street for RMB 5,000,000. On April 25, 2002, the Sichuan High People's Court issued civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2-2, confirming that the 38 buildings in Shabanqiao Residential Area were acquired by Chenghua District Xinhua Real Estate Development Company; on June 13 of the same year, it issued civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2-4, confirming that the 7,000.04 square meters of land use rights at Tianyashi South Street were acquired by the Jinjiang District Construction Bureau of Chengdu. After deducting auction commissions and giving priority to paying the appraisal fees advanced by Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group, the remaining auction proceeds amounted to RMB 5,100,000.

The Sichuan High People's Court distributed the RMB 5,100,000 in auction proceeds according to the debt ratio of Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group and the other execution applicant, Sichuan Zhanwang Industrial Company. Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group was entitled to receive RMB 4,584,400. Because the Sichuan High People's Court and the Mianyang Intermediate People's Court, among others, had accepted multiple cases in which Jiangyou Credit Cooperative was the execution debtor, the Sichuan High People's Court distributed the RMB 4,584,400 that the Liquidation Group was entitled to receive according to the debt ratio of its creditors, with the remaining RMB 1,799,400 paid to the Liquidation Group. On March 28, 2005, based on the application of Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group, the Sichuan High People's Court issued civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2-5, terminating the execution of the case and issuing a creditor's certificate.

The Sichuan High People's Court held that: In the execution of the case between Jiangyou Credit Cooperative and Luoshu Real Estate Company, Sichuan Zhanwang Industrial Company also applied to the court for compulsory enforcement of the debt owed by Luoshu Real Estate Company, holding an expired notarized creditor's document. Where the court, without obtaining the consent of the execution applicant and the execution debtor, without a public auction, when other creditors had already applied for distribution, and without specifying the specific amount of the transfer, issued civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2 to transfer the land use rights and buildings of Luoshu Real Estate Company to Jiangyou Credit Cooperative as compensation, this did not comply with legal provisions. The court's civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2-1, which corrected the substantive content of civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2 on the grounds of a clerical error, was indeed inappropriate, but the substantive handling was correct. Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group also failed to provide evidence of a voluntary agreement on the transfer with Luoshu Real Estate Company. Because Luoshu Real Estate Company was insolvent, and its multiple mature creditors applied for enforcement, the Sichuan High People's Court lawfully distributed the company's property according to the debt ratio of its creditors, which was not improper. The court repeatedly organized consultations with the Jiangyou City People's Government, the Jiangyou Sub-branch of the People's Bank of China, and Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group to determine the reserve price for the auction of the land use rights and buildings. Under the legal provisions in force at that time, the reserve price for the auction did not require the consent of the execution applicant or the execution debtor. Because the execution debtor's property had legal defects, after two failed auctions, the third auction was successfully concluded at RMB 6,000,000. The appraisal agency and auction agency commissioned by the Sichuan High People's Court were lawful, and the appraisal and auction processes complied with legal procedures; there was no intentional diminution of the value of the execution debtor's property or illegal disposal. Therefore, the court's enforcement acts were not improper and did not cause direct loss to Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group. Pursuant to Article 31 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 12 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Confirmation Cases for State Compensation by People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), on July 17, 2009, it rendered ruling (2009) Chuan Fa Que Zi No. 1, deciding not to confirm that the official acts of the Sichuan High People's Court in executing Luoshu Real Estate Company were illegal.

The applicant for confirmation, Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group, dissatisfied with the ruling of the court of first instance, filed a petition with this Court, requesting the revocation of the ruling of the Sichuan High People's Court (2009) Chuan Fa Que Zi No. 1 and confirmation that the acts of the court in issuing civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2-1 and disposing of the property already transferred to the Liquidation Group were illegal. The main grounds for the petition were: 1. The civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2-1 issued by the Sichuan High People's Court, which altered the substantive content of civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2 on the grounds of a clerical error, was illegal; 2. Jiangyou Credit Cooperative applied for property preservation and enforcement first, and the Sichuan High People's Court's distribution of the RMB 5,100,000 in auction proceeds according to the debt ratio between it and Sichuan Zhanwang Industrial Company violated Article 88 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Execution Work of People's Courts; 3. The Sichuan High People's Court's distribution of the RMB 4,584,400 that the Liquidation Group was entitled to receive according to the debt ratio of its creditors violated Article 24 of the Regulations of the State Council on the Cancellation of Financial Institutions and Articles 1 and 3 of the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Trial of Related Civil Cases During the Rectification of Urban Credit Cooperatives (Fa [2002] No. 252); 4. The confirmation of the auction reserve price by the Jiangyou City People's Government could not represent the views of the Liquidation Group.

Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group did not raise any objection to the facts found by the court of first instance in its petition.

This Court additionally finds that: During the enforcement process, the legal representative of Luoshu Real Estate Company, Wang Shunxian, was missing, the company had ceased operations, and apart from the sealed-up land use rights and buildings, there was no other property available for enforcement. On March 28, 2000, Sichuan Zhanwang Industrial Company raised an oral objection to civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2, requesting participation in the distribution, and submitted a written objection on March 30 of the same year. Chengdu Jinxin Real Estate Development Company submitted a written enforcement objection to the Sichuan High People's Court on April 21, 2000, claiming ownership of the 11 buildings in Lianhua Residential Area and providing building ownership certificates as evidence; the court confirmed that the above buildings did not belong to the execution debtor Luoshu Real Estate Company. The second appraisal report of Sichuan Tonghe Accounting Firm stated that the restrictive conditions for the use of the appraisal results were: Luoshu Real Estate Company had outstanding land concession fees of RMB 1,653,182.6, relocation costs of RMB 12,326,600, and the properties had not been transferred. On March 13 and April 5, 2002, Sichuan Hanya Cultural Treasures Auction House published auction announcements in the Chengdu Commercial Newspaper for the 38 buildings in Shabanqiao Residential Area and the 7,000.04 square meters of land use rights at Tianyashi South Street. During the process of distributing the RMB 4,584,400 that Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group was entitled to receive according to the debt ratio of its depositors who had applied for participation in the distribution, after receiving the notice Fa [2002] No. 252 issued by the Supreme People's Court, the Sichuan High People's Court paid the remaining RMB 1,799,400 to the Liquidation Group.

It is further found that: After Jiangyou Credit Cooperative, due to insolvency and the flight of its responsible persons, experienced a serious payment crisis starting from the end of 1997, the governments of Sichuan Province, Mianyang City, and Jiangyou City fully intervened in its loan recovery and payment work. On September 28, 2000, Jiangyou Credit Cooperative was approved by the People's Bank of China to suspend operations for rectification. On April 19, 2002, the Jiangyou City People's Government issued a document establishing the Leading Group for the Cancellation of Jiangyou City Credit Cooperative and a Liquidation Working Group. On May 16 of the same year, with the consent of the Sichuan Provincial People's Government and the approval of the People's Bank of China, Jiangyou Credit Cooperative was cancelled.

Opinion of the Court: (1) In the loan dispute case between Jiangyou Credit Cooperative and Luoshu Real Estate Company, the effective civil judgment (1998) Chuan Jing Er Chu Zi No. 70 of the Sichuan High People's Court ordered Luoshu Real Estate Company to repay Jiangyou Credit Cooperative the principal of RMB 34,000,000 in loans plus interest. During the enforcement of the case, Sichuan Zhanwang Industrial Company also applied for compulsory enforcement of a debt of RMB 3,824,000 owed by Luoshu Real Estate Company, holding an expired notarized creditor's document, and the Sichuan High People's Court opened a case for enforcement. Under circumstances where the sealed-up property of Luoshu Real Estate Company was insufficient to satisfy all its debts and there was no other property available for enforcement, the Sichuan High People's Court, without obtaining the consent of the execution applicant and the execution debtor and without appraising the value, issued civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2 to transfer all of the execution debtor's property to one of the execution applicants as compensation. This handling was indeed improper. Subsequently, the court issued civil ruling (2000) Chuan Zhi Zi No. 2-1 on the grounds of correcting a clerical error to correct the main text of the original ruling. There was indeed a procedural defect. However, the substantive result of the handling in that ruling did not cause actual loss to the lawful rights of Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group. (2) Article 88, paragraph 1, of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Execution Work of People's Courts provides that creditors are to be satisfied in the order of the measures of preservation and enforcement, but the premise is that the debtor has full capacity to satisfy the debts. Since the execution debtor Luoshu Real Estate Company was insolvent and had voluntarily ceased operations, this case should apply Article 96 of that judicial interpretation, with multiple creditors sharing the execution proceeds on a pro rata basis. (3) As for the claim raised by Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group in its petition that the Sichuan High People's Court's continued distribution of the auction proceeds it was entitled to receive violated the Regulations of the State Council on the Cancellation of Financial Institutions and the Supreme People's Court's Notice Fa [2002] No. 252, because Jiangyou Credit Cooperative was indeed the execution debtor in multiple other certificate-of-deposit dispute cases, the act of the Sichuan High People's Court in continuing to distribute the auction proceeds before receiving the Supreme People's Court's Notice Fa [2002] No. 252 did not cause loss to Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group and did not violate the provisions of the above regulations and notice. (4) Regarding the reason raised by Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group in its petition that the confirmation of the auction reserve price by the Jiangyou City People's Government could not represent the views of the Liquidation Group, upon examination, after Jiangyou Credit Cooperative experienced the flight of its responsible persons and a serious payment crisis, the governments of Sichuan Province, Mianyang City, and Jiangyou City fully intervened in its loan recovery and payment work and appointed relevant responsible persons to handle the incident. Therefore, the Sichuan High People's Court's several consultations with relevant responsible persons of the Jiangyou City People's Government and the commissioning of the auction of the land use rights and buildings based on the reserve price determined by the Jiangyou City People's Government were not improper. In summary, the ruling of the Sichuan High People's Court (2009) Chuan Fa Que Zi No. 1 was correct and should be affirmed. The petition reasons of the applicant for confirmation, Jiangyou Credit Cooperative Liquidation Group, cannot be established and should be dismissed. Pursuant to Article 31 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 12 and Article 17, paragraph 2, of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Confirmation Cases for State Compensation by People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), it is ruled as follows:

The petition is dismissed, and the ruling of the Sichuan High People's Court (2009) Chuan Fa Que Zi No. 1 is affirmed.

This ruling becomes legally effective upon service.

Presiding Judge: Hu Shihao
Acting Judge: Gao Jingwen
Acting Judge: Liang Qing
November 27, 2009
Clerk: Cai Zhiwen
